What the records show in between those two census years and his death is nothing: nearly five decades pass with no marriage record, no appearances in the 1870, 1880, or 1900 censuses, and no Civil War service record, even though his son-in-law signed the death certificate — proof he had at least one married child. There are also two unresolved disputes woven through the earliest events: one about whether he was born in Ireland or Pennsylvania, and another about whether the five-year-old in the Thomas Flynn household is truly the same person who died in 1908. The timeline holds together across the 1850–1860 decade but cannot be called settled until those two conflicts are decided.

The next step is to take both open disputes to conflict-resolution, which will weigh the census evidence against the death certificate and decide which record best identifies the 1850 child.
